senses.definition: (military) A unit of thirty to forty soldiers typically commanded by a lieutenant and forming part of a company.

quotes.text: Needless to say, one's seat must be booked in advance and a platoon of urbane officials, one to each door of the train, awaits passengers to usher them to their seats and relieve them of their bulkier baggage.
quotes.reference: 1960 March, G. Freeman Allen, “Europe's most luxurious express - the "Settebello"”, in Trains Illustrated, page 140:

senses.definition: A subdivision of a fire company, led by a captain or lieutenant.
A group of self-driving vehicles travelling in a close convoy and communicating electronically with each other.
(education, historical) A group of children in the platoon grouping education system.
(baseball) To alternate starts with a teammate of opposite handedness, depending on the handedness of the opposing pitcher
examples: Taylor has been hitting poorly against left-handers, and Morgan has been hitting poorly against right-handers, so they will platoon.

senses.definition: (sports) To specialize in a particular position or playing style.

quotes.text: You must understand the rules of football in 1939. There was no platooning, so each man played both offense and defense.

senses.definition: Of self-driving vehicles: to travel in a close convoy, each vehicle communicating electronically with the others.
